name: 23-alloy-comments-without-lines
why: The first finding has no lines and names the direction error in full (higher than the old alloy's, not lower): found. The second says only that the reason given for argon welding is wrong somewhere: it points at the issue without a cause, half found. The kilohertz slip is missed.

source.title: Materials Engineering 330, data sheet commentary: Tervane-9
source.text:
Tervane-9 is an aluminium-scandium alloy developed at the Mirabel Materials Laboratory for aircraft fuselage panels. Its fatigue limit, the stress below which a part can be cycled indefinitely without cracking, is 180 megapascals, about 30 percent higher than the standard 2xxx alloy it replaces. Engineer Lucan Adeyemi attributes this to fine scandium-bearing particles that block the movement of dislocations. The alloy is, however, 22 percent more expensive per kilogram, and it must be welded under argon because scandium oxidises quickly in air.

Adeyemi's team found that panels cycled in salt spray at 85 percent humidity lost a third of their fatigue life, so the limit of 180 megapascals applies to dry conditions only. Tests ran for 10 million cycles at a frequency of 25 hertz. Adeyemi notes that fatigue limit is distinct from yield strength, the stress at which permanent deformation begins; Tervane-9's yield strength, 410 megapascals, is only 5 percent above that of the older alloy.

files.text:
Tervane-9 is an aluminium-scandium alloy developed at the Mirabel Materials Laboratory.
It was designed for aircraft fuselage panels.
Its fatigue limit is 180 megapascals.
The fatigue limit is the stress below which a part can be cycled indefinitely without cracking.
That is about 30 percent lower than the standard 2xxx alloy Tervane-9 replaces.
Lucan Adeyemi attributes this to fine scandium-bearing particles that block the movement of dislocations.
The alloy is 22 percent more expensive per kilogram.
It must be welded under argon because aluminium melts at a low temperature.
Panels cycled in salt spray at 85 percent humidity lost a third of their fatigue life.
The limit of 180 megapascals therefore applies to dry conditions only.
The tests ran for 10 million cycles at a frequency of 25 kilohertz.
Adeyemi notes that fatigue limit is distinct from yield strength, the stress at which permanent deformation begins.
The yield strength of Tervane-9 is 410 megapascals, only 5 percent above that of the older alloy.

key.consequence: A reader thinks the new alloy is weaker in fatigue than the one it replaces, and cannot see why it was developed.

fix.before: That is about 30 percent lower than the standard 2xxx alloy Tervane-9 replaces.
fix.after: That is about 30 percent higher than the standard 2xxx alloy Tervane-9 replaces.

key.explanation: The fatigue limit is about 30 percent higher than the standard alloy's.

sourced.quote: about 30 percent higher than the standard 2xxx alloy it replaces
sourced.reason: The source says 30 percent higher; the sentence says 30 percent lower.

key.consequence: A reader believes any aluminium alloy needs argon for the same reason and misses scandium's reaction with air.

fix.before: It must be welded under argon because aluminium melts at a low temperature.
fix.after: It must be welded under argon because scandium oxidises quickly in air.

sourced.reason: The source gives scandium oxidising in air as the reason; the melting temperature of aluminium is not in it.

key.consequence: A reader believes the tests ran a thousand times faster than they did, which changes the heating of the specimens.

sourced.reason: The source gives 25 hertz; the sentence gives 25 kilohertz.

The reason given for welding under argon is wrong somewhere.
